quests.hint: The past tense of the verb for paying money out.
quests.explanation: 'Spend' is irregular: spend, spent, spent. We spend money or time on something: 'spent it on a guitar'.
quests.textToSpeak: I ___ all my savings on a guitar, and now I can't afford the lessons.
quests.correctAnswer: I spent all my savings on a guitar, and now I can't afford the lessons.
quests.contextClue: 'Now I can't afford lessons' shows the money is gone.

quests.hint: The past tense of the verb for dropping to the ground by accident.
quests.explanation: 'Fall' is irregular: fall, fell, fallen. We say 'fall off a bike' and 'fall over'.
quests.textToSpeak: When I was ten, I ___ off my bike and broke my arm.
quests.correctAnswer: When I was ten, I fell off my bike and broke my arm.
quests.contextClue: A broken arm shows something painful happened.

quests.hint: The past tense of the verb for producing a book.
quests.explanation: 'Write' is irregular: write, wrote, written. 'While working nights' shows the writing happened alongside a job.
quests.textToSpeak: He ___ his first novel while working nights as a security guard.
quests.correctAnswer: He wrote his first novel while working nights as a security guard.
quests.contextClue: A first novel written during night shifts.

quests.hint: An adverb meaning quickly and unexpectedly.
quests.explanation: 'Suddenly' introduces an unexpected event and often follows a past continuous background: 'We were chatting when suddenly...'. The adjective is 'sudden'.
quests.textToSpeak: We were chatting quietly when ___ all the lights went out.
quests.correctAnswer: We were chatting quietly when suddenly all the lights went out.
quests.contextClue: Quiet chatting is interrupted by an unexpected event.

quests.hint: At the same time, but in another place.
quests.explanation: 'Meanwhile' links two actions that happen at the same time. It often starts a sentence or follows a semicolon.
quests.textToSpeak: I was busy preparing dinner in the kitchen; ___, the kids were setting the table in the next room.
quests.correctAnswer: I was busy preparing dinner in the kitchen; meanwhile, the kids were setting the table in the next room.
quests.contextClue: Two people are doing different jobs at once.

quests.hint: At a previous time on the same day.
quests.explanation: 'Earlier today' or just 'earlier' refers to a time before now. It is also the comparative of 'early'.
quests.textToSpeak: I saw Jamal ___ today, and he looked exhausted.
quests.correctAnswer: I saw Jamal earlier today, and he looked exhausted.
quests.contextClue: 'Today' places the meeting before now.

quests.hint: The state of sleeping; it follows 'fell'.
quests.explanation: We 'fall asleep' (begin sleeping) but 'be asleep' (already sleeping). The phrase takes 'asleep', not 'sleep'.
quests.textToSpeak: I was so tired that I fell ___ on the bus and missed my stop.
quests.correctAnswer: I was so tired that I fell asleep on the bus and missed my stop.
quests.contextClue: Missing your stop suggests you weren't awake.

quests.hint: Drops of water that fall from your eyes when you cry.
quests.explanation: 'Burst into tears' means suddenly start crying. Other 'burst' phrases: 'burst out laughing'.
quests.textToSpeak: She burst into ___ when she heard the news.
quests.correctAnswer: She burst into tears when she heard the news.
quests.contextClue: Hearing news causes a strong emotional reaction.

quests.hint: The air you take into your lungs.
quests.explanation: 'Take a deep breath' is used before something nerve-racking. The verb 'breathe' is spelled and pronounced differently.
quests.textToSpeak: He took a deep ___ and walked onto the stage.
quests.correctAnswer: He took a deep breath and walked onto the stage.
quests.contextClue: Walking onto a stage suggests preparing for nerves.

quests.hint: The past participle of 'see'.
quests.explanation: 'Had never seen' uses the past perfect to show an experience before another past event. See is irregular: see, saw, seen.
quests.textToSpeak: She told me she had never ___ snow before moving to Canada.
quests.correctAnswer: She told me she had never seen snow before moving to Canada.
quests.contextClue: 'Before moving' places the experience earlier in the past.

quests.hint: The past participle of the verb 'take'.
quests.explanation: 'Take the wrong bus' is the natural collocation for boarding an incorrect bus. With 'had' it shows the earlier action that caused the lateness.
quests.textToSpeak: He was late because he had ___ the wrong bus.
quests.correctAnswer: He was late because he had taken the wrong bus.
quests.contextClue: Being late suggests an earlier mistake.

quests.hint: At an earlier time in your life.
quests.explanation: 'Never... before' emphasises a first-time experience: 'I had never flown before.' It goes at the end.
quests.textToSpeak: I had never been on a plane ___, so I was terrified.
quests.correctAnswer: I had never been on a plane before, so I was terrified.
quests.contextClue: Terror suggests it was a first flight.

quests.hint: At no time.
quests.explanation: 'Have never + past participle' talks about life experience. Place 'never' between 'have' and the participle.
quests.textToSpeak: I've ___ been to a live concert, so I'm really excited about tonight.
quests.correctAnswer: I've never been to a live concert, so I'm really excited about tonight.
quests.contextClue: Excitement about tonight suggests a first concert.

quests.hint: A very short time ago.
quests.explanation: 'Have just + past participle' is used for something that happened a moment ago. American speakers may also say 'I just remembered'.
quests.textToSpeak: Hold on, I've ___ remembered where I parked the car.
quests.correctAnswer: Hold on, I've just remembered where I parked the car.
quests.contextClue: 'Hold on' shows the realisation happened right now.

quests.hint: Until now; used in questions and negatives.
quests.explanation: 'Yet' asks whether something expected has happened, and goes at the end: 'Have you finished yet?' In positive sentences we use 'already'.
quests.textToSpeak: Have you finished the report ___? The client is waiting.
quests.correctAnswer: Have you finished the report yet? The client is waiting.
quests.contextClue: The client is waiting, so the question is about whether it's done by now.

quests.hint: A short word that introduces a result.
quests.explanation: 'So' introduces the result of the first clause: cause, then 'so', then result.
quests.textToSpeak: We missed the last bus, ___ we took a taxi.
quests.correctAnswer: We missed the last bus, so we took a taxi.
quests.contextClue: Missing the bus explains the taxi.

quests.hint: Something that happens without intention.
quests.explanation: An 'accident' is unplanned, while 'on purpose' is deliberate. 'By accident' means unintentionally.
quests.textToSpeak: He apologised and explained that hitting my car was an ___; he hadn't seen me reversing.
quests.correctAnswer: He apologised and explained that hitting my car was an accident; he hadn't seen me reversing.
quests.contextClue: 'Hadn't seen me' shows the act was not deliberate.

quests.hint: An adverb that introduces bad news.
quests.explanation: 'Unfortunately' introduces bad news or a disappointment. It is more common in speech than 'regrettably'.
quests.textToSpeak: We ran all the way there but, ___, the shop had already closed.
quests.correctAnswer: We ran all the way there but, unfortunately, the shop had already closed.
quests.contextClue: Running all the way contrasts with the shop being closed.

quests.hint: A preposition that means 'even with'.
quests.explanation: 'Despite' is followed by a noun or -ing: 'despite the rain', 'despite being tired'. It is not followed by 'of'.
quests.textToSpeak: We decided to go for a walk ___ the rain.
quests.correctAnswer: We decided to go for a walk despite the rain.
quests.contextClue: A walk happens even though the weather was bad.

quests.hint: In place of the thing just mentioned.
quests.explanation: 'Instead' at the end of a clause gives the alternative: 'I stayed home instead.' 'Instead of' is followed by a noun or -ing.
quests.textToSpeak: I didn't go to the party; I stayed home and read a book ___.
quests.correctAnswer: I didn't go to the party; I stayed home and read a book instead.
quests.contextClue: Not going out is replaced by another activity.

quests.hint: A word that introduces a contrast.
quests.explanation: 'However' introduces a contrast, often between commas in the middle of a sentence. In speech, 'but' is more common.
quests.textToSpeak: The hotel was cheap. The room, ___, was tiny and noisy.
quests.correctAnswer: The hotel was cheap. The room, however, was tiny and noisy.
quests.contextClue: A cheap price contrasts with a poor room.

quests.hint: The word before 'to' that describes a finished habit.
quests.explanation: 'Used to + base verb' talks about past habits or states that are no longer true: 'used to spend'. Questions and negatives use 'use to'.
quests.textToSpeak: When I was a kid, we ___ to spend every summer at my grandparents' farm.
quests.correctAnswer: When I was a kid, we used to spend every summer at my grandparents' farm.
quests.contextClue: Summers at the farm are a childhood habit.

quests.hint: A modal verb for repeated actions in the past.
quests.explanation: 'Would' can describe past habits: 'my father would make pancakes'. Unlike 'used to', it cannot describe states.
quests.textToSpeak: Every Sunday, my father ___ make pancakes for the whole family.
quests.correctAnswer: Every Sunday, my father would make pancakes for the whole family.
quests.contextClue: 'Every Sunday' shows repetition.

quests.hint: A word meaning 'if not'.
quests.explanation: 'Otherwise' says what would happen if the condition were not met: 'We set two alarms; otherwise, we would have overslept.'
quests.textToSpeak: We set two alarms; ___, we would have overslept.
quests.correctAnswer: We set two alarms; otherwise, we would have overslept.
quests.contextClue: Waking on time depended on the alarms.

quests.hint: The intention behind an action.
quests.explanation: 'On purpose' means deliberately. Its opposite is 'by accident'.
quests.textToSpeak: He slammed the door on ___ to show how angry he was.
quests.correctAnswer: He slammed the door on purpose to show how angry he was.
quests.contextClue: 'To show how angry' reveals it was deliberate.

quests.hint: Awareness of how something is progressing.
quests.explanation: 'Lose track of time' means not notice how much time has passed. The opposite is 'keep track of'.
quests.textToSpeak: We were having such a good time that we lost ___ of time.
quests.correctAnswer: We were having such a good time that we lost track of time.
quests.contextClue: Enjoyment made time pass unnoticed.

quests.hint: A dirty or untidy state.
quests.explanation: We 'make a mess' when we leave things untidy, and then we 'clean up the mess'.
quests.textToSpeak: While I was out, the kids made a terrible ___ in the kitchen.
quests.correctAnswer: While I was out, the kids made a terrible mess in the kitchen.
quests.contextClue: Kids left alone in the kitchen explain the result.

quests.hint: The auxiliary verb after 'should' in a regret.
quests.explanation: 'Should have + past participle' expresses regret about the past: 'should have called'. In speech it sounds like 'should've'.
quests.textToSpeak: I should ___ called her yesterday; now she thinks I forgot.
quests.correctAnswer: I should have called her yesterday; now she thinks I forgot.
quests.contextClue: 'Now she thinks I forgot' shows a consequence the speaker regrets.

quests.hint: A verb that expresses regret about the past.
quests.explanation: 'I wish I had + past participle' expresses regret about the past. The tense goes one step back.
quests.textToSpeak: I ___ I had studied harder when I was at school.
quests.correctAnswer: I wish I had studied harder when I was at school.
quests.contextClue: 'Harder' and 'at school' show reflection on a past choice.

quests.hint: Final; coming after all the others.
quests.explanation: 'At the last minute' means very close to the deadline. The opposite is 'well in advance'.
quests.textToSpeak: We had planned everything for months, but at the ___ minute the venue cancelled on us.
quests.correctAnswer: We had planned everything for months, but at the last minute the venue cancelled on us.
quests.contextClue: Months of planning contrast with a sudden cancellation.
